Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz / 40 fps lock gives smooth, tear-free gameplay and is the most stable target for this CPU-bound game in mid-game saves. Expect drops into the low 30s in very dense factory areas — consider switching to Max Battery settings if your save is heavily built-out.

profiles.Summary: Satisfactory is a demanding open-world factory builder that stresses the CPU heavily as factories grow, making it one of the more challenging games for the Steam Deck's Zen 2 CPU; it runs on the Deck as Verified but performance degrades significantly in large, complex factory builds. At default settings the game can hover around 30 fps in early/mid-game but will drop in late-game factory areas, so lower settings and a locked frame rate are strongly recommended.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1650 / RX 570, which closely matches the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU) and the known CPU-heavy nature of Satisfactory's factory simulation. On your first run, test in an early-game area and again in your most complex factory area — CPU frame drops in late-game are the primary limiter, and you should lower the frame cap or TDP accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and use Deck FSR to upscale, keeping the GPU mostly idle so the CPU can handle factory logic. Battery savings are significant but late-game factory areas will still cause dips below 30 fps regardless of GPU settings.

KnownIssues: Late-game large factories cause severe CPU-bound frame drops that no GPU setting can fix — performance is highly save-dependent.
The game is CPU-intensive by nature; as factory complexity grows, frame rates will decline regardless of graphics settings.
Online multiplayer is noticeably more demanding than solo play and may require dropping to Max Battery settings to stay stable.
No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparisons.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with Medium settings and full TDP gives the best visual clarity the Deck can offer, but 60 fps is not reliably sustainable — frame rates will vary widely with factory complexity. If the game feels unstable, drop to the Optimal profile's 40 Hz lock.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives a smooth, tear-free experience that holds well in early-to-mid game; expect dips into the low 30s in heavily built-up factory areas — drop shadows to Low if needed.

profiles.Summary: Satisfactory is a demanding open-world factory builder built on Unreal Engine 5; the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU sits right at the minimum spec class, so expect modest settings and FSR to maintain playable frame rates, especially as factories grow larger. The game runs well under Proton with a Verified rating, though performance will degrade noticeably in late-game mega-factory areas.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1650 class GPU, matching the Deck's RDNA 2), the UE5 engine's known overhead, and the Deck hardware spec. On your first run, check frame rates in an open area and again inside your first mid-sized factory — if the factory scene drops below 25 fps, switch to Max Battery settings and lower View Distance further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 and upscaling with FSR keeps the GPU load low enough for the 8 W TDP limit; battery life will shorten in large factories where the CPU becomes the bottleneck regardless of GPU settings.

KnownIssues: Factory complexity (conveyor belts, machines, power lines) causes significant CPU-side performance drops in late game that no GPU setting can fix.
The game requires an internet connection for multiplayer; co-op sessions will further stress the Deck's CPU and reduce frame rates.
No native Linux build — runs via Proton, which adds a small overhead; Proton Experimental is generally recommended for UE5 titles.
UI text and menus may be small on the 1280x800 screen, though the game lists Adjustable Text Size as a feature.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 1280x800 at medium settings with no TDP cap extracts the most from the hardware, but 60 fps is not stable in complex factory scenes — the cap acts as a ceiling rather than a floor, and battery life is short.
